record.original_question: Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A regular abstract polytope is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ with a strictly monotone rank function whose elements (called faces) of ranks $-1$ and $n$ are unique, such that every maximal chain (flag) has the same length, $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, the diamond condition holds, and the automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on the flags. A realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in a metric space $X$ is a mapping $\beta$ from the set of vertices (rank-0 faces) of $\mathcal{P}$ into $X$ such that every automorphism in $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ induces an isometry of $X$ permuting the image vertices in the appropriate way, with the realization extended in the natural recursive manner to higher-rank faces. In Euclidean space, a well-developed theory exists: the cone of realizations decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible (pure) realizations indexed by the irreducible orthogonal representations of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$, and there are explicit Wythoff-style and orthogonality (cosine vector) relations.

Develop an analogous theory of realizations of regular abstract polytopes in hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n$ (and, more generally, in real, complex, or quaternionic hyperbolic spaces). Specifically:

(a) Formulate the correct notion of a (faithful, symmetric) realization of a regular polytope in hyperbolic space, accounting for the noncompact isometry group $\mathrm{O}^+(n,1)$ in place of $\mathrm{O}(n+1)$.

(b) Establish a decomposition or structure theorem for the space of all such realizations analogous to the orthogonal-representation decomposition in the Euclidean/spherical case, using the representation theory of the relevant indefinite-orthogonal or noncompact Lie groups.

(c) Identify which regular polytopes admit faithful hyperbolic realizations, characterize the pure (irreducible) hyperbolic realizations, and derive the corresponding cosine-type orthogonality relations, including criteria for when realizations are discrete.
artifact.status_search_result: The Euclidean theory of realizations of regular polytopes (McMullen and Schulte) is well-established, and there are extensive results on regular tessellations and Coxeter polytopes in hyperbolic space. However, no general theory of realizations of regular abstract polytopes in hyperbolic spaces analogous to the Euclidean case appears in the literature; the problem is an open program rather than a settled theorem.

status_evidence.title: Realizations of Polytopes (Chapter 4) - Geometric Regular Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: A realization of a regular incidence-polytope is given by an image of its vertices under a mapping into some euclidean space such that every automorphism induces an isometry.
status_evidence.claim: The standard realization theory is developed in Euclidean (and spherical) settings; an analogous hyperbolic theory is not the standard framework.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Schulte handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of regular polytopes and tessellations in spherical, euclidean or hyperbolic space remains an active area.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolic regular structures are studied case-by-case, but a unified realization theory parallel to the Euclidean one is not established.
